## 2. Chapters

### `ch13` — Defensive Positioning · *Where to stand before the pitch, and why*
**minutes:** 11 · **quizIds:** `q1301`–`q1308`

**Objectives**
- After this chapter you can name the default alignment and the assumption it makes.
- After this chapter you can choose infield-in, double-play depth, bunt defence, or no-doubles from the score, the inning, and the runners.
- After this chapter you can say what each of those alignments buys and what it gives up.
- After this chapter you can explain who covers second on a steal and how the middle infielders decide.
- After this chapter you can adjust a step for hitter tendency and for the count.

**Sections (14)**

| # | type | heading |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | prose | Standard is the default — and it assumes nothing special |
| 2 | diagram | Standard alignment (`alignment: 'standard'`) |
| 3 | prose | Infield in, and double-play depth |

Trap cases in the widget: up-big with R3 (not infield-in); R2 and two outs (not infield-in); slap hitter / sac-fly threat (of-shallow, not infield-in).

### `ch14` — Cutoffs, Relays & Backups · *Ball, base, backup — nobody stands still*
**minutes:** 14 · **quizIds:** `q1401`–`q1408`

**Objectives**
- After this chapter you can assign ball, base, or backup to all nine players on a given batted ball.
- After this chapter you can name the cutoff or relay by hit location — left, centre, right — and the first baseman’s job on a throw home.
- After this chapter you can set a cutoff in a straight line, two-thirds of the way to the outfielder, arms up.
- After this chapter you can name the backup jobs: pitcher at third and home, right field at first, outfielders behind each other.
- After this chapter you can say what happens when a cutoff is missed, and why the target position — not the outfielder — calls the throw.

**Sections (12)**

| # | type | heading |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | prose | Three jobs. Nine players. No spectators. |
| 2 | diagram | Ground ball to short — nobody on (`roles` + `arrows`) |
| 3 | prose | Who is the cut, who is the relay, who is the trailer |
| 4 | diagram | Single to left — cutoff to second (`roles` + `arrows`) |
| 5 | diagram | Single to centre — first is the cut to home (`roles` + `arrows`) |
| 6 | diagram | Extra-base hit to right — relay and trailer (`roles` + `arrows`) |
| 7 | prose | Line, arms up, and the catcher’s voice |
| 8 | example | The cut that was not there |
| 9 | terms | — |
| 10 | interactive | Assign the nine (`assignTheNine`, 9 cases) |
| 11 | coachnote | Install one scenario, then add the map |
| 12 | keypoints | Take this with you |

Four `field` diagrams carry `roles`. Cutoff/relay is taught as a **base** job in the three-job system: covering a designated intercept, not fielding the batted ball.

### `ch15` — Baserunning IQ · *Leads, reads, steals, and first-and-third*
**minutes:** 12 · **quizIds:** `q1501`–`q1508`

**Objectives**
- After this chapter you can tell a primary lead from a secondary lead, and which divisions allow either.
- After this chapter you can read a pitcher’s move as pitch, pickoff, or balk, and say what “steal on the pitcher” means.
- After this chapter you can freeze on a line drive, tag up on first contact, and change the read from first, second, and third.
- After this chapter you can describe first-and-third from both sides, including the Little League catcher fake-throw ban.
- After this chapter you can say when to pick up the base coach and what the windmill, the stop, and the slide signal mean.

### `ch16` — Bunting & Small Ball · *Moving the runner, and when it is worth an out*
**minutes:** 11 · **quizIds:** `q1601`–`q1608`

**Objectives**
- After this chapter you can describe square versus pivot, the pinching grip, bat level, and why you bunt only strikes.
- After this chapter you can name sacrifice, drag, push, safety squeeze, suicide squeeze, and slash by intent.
- After this chapter you can assign bunt defence — who charges, who covers — and describe the wheel play.
- After this chapter you can decide whether a sacrifice is worth the out given score, inning, outs, and the hitter on deck.
- After this chapter you can say why higher levels bunt less, and where the no-leadoff rule makes a sacrifice a poor trade.

## 5. `assignTheNine` role table

Three-job mapping used throughout: **ball** = fielder of the batted ball; **base** = covering a bag **or** occupying cutoff/relay; **backup** = behind a throw or a teammate.

| Case | Situation | P | C | 1B | 2B | 3B | SS | LF | CF | RF | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gb-ss-empty` | GB to SS, empty, 0 out | backup | backup | base | base | base | **ball** | backup | backup | backup | `infield-play` (throw to first); `outfield-play` (RF backs first, CF second, LF third); engine: catcher trails first with nobody on |
| `gb-ss-r1-dp` | GB to SS, R1, 0 out, DP | backup | base | base | base | base | **ball** | backup | backup | backup | `infield-play` (SS feed, 2B pivot); catcher covers home once a runner is on; same OF backups |
| `gb-1b-pitcher-covers` | GB wide of 1B, empty | **base** | backup | **ball** | base | base | backup | backup | backup | backup | `infield-play` (3-1: pitcher covers first); SS backs second; C/RF back first |
| `gb-3b-r3-infield-in` | GB to 3B, R3, 0 out, infield in | backup | base | base | backup | **ball** | base | backup | backup | backup | `defensive-positioning` / `defensive-strategy` (infield in, play at plate); P backs home with R3; 2B helps first, no force at second |
| `single-lf-empty` | Single LF, empty, throw to 2B | backup | base | base | base | base | **base** (cut) | **ball** | backup | backup | `cutoffs-and-relays` (SS cut on a ball to left; 2B covers second); `outfield-play` (CF backs LF; far OF backs the throw-target base) |
| `single-cf-r3-home` | Single CF, R3, 1 out, throw home | backup | base | **base** (cut) | base | base | base | backup | **ball** | backup | Brief + `defensive-strategy` (1B is cut on throws home); 2B covers first because 1B left; P backs home; OF backs CF |
| `xbh-rf-r1` | XBH RF, R1, throw to third | backup | base | **backup** (trailer) | **base** (relay) | base | base | backup | backup | **ball** | `cutoffs-and-relays` (2B relay to right, SS covers second, 3B at third, 1B trails); P backs third; CF backs RF; far OF backs second |
| `line-cf-r1` | LD to CF caught, R1, 0 out | backup | base | base | **base** (cut to 1st) | base | base | backup | **ball** | backup | `tagging-up-and-reads` (liner double-off); 2B is the cut on a throw back to first from CF; OF backs the catch |
| `gap-lc-r2` | Gap LCF, R2, relay home | backup | base | base | base | base | **base** (relay) | backup | **ball** | backup | `cutoffs-and-relays` (SS primary relay on extra-base to left, runner scoring from second; 2B covers second; 3B trail if a second runner goes to third); P backs home |

Cases 2, 4, 6, 8, and 9 have runners on. Mix is four grounders, two singles, two extra-base/gap, one line drive.

## 6. KB pages read

**Named in the brief:** `defensive-positioning`, `defensive-strategy`, `cutoffs-and-relays`, `outfield-play`, `infield-play`, `base-stealing-and-leadoffs`, `first-and-third-situations`, `tagging-up-and-reads`, `base-coaching-duties`, `holding-runners-and-pickoffs`, `bunting`, `offensive-strategy`

**Also read, because the named pages were thin:** `baserunning-fundamentals` (primary/secondary), `sign-systems-and-communication` (who covers second), `drills/situational-bunt-coverages` (wheel), `drills/slash-bunt-hit`, `drills/primary-lead`. BUILD-PLAN also points at `baseball-app/js/engine.js`; that is the source of the nobody-on catcher-backs-first rule and the 3-1 pitcher-covers-first rule.

**Where the KB did not fully answer, and how it was handled**
- Cutoff vs relay: `cutoffs-and-relays` makes SS/2B the relay on extra-base hits; the brief and `defensive-strategy` make 1B/3B the cut, with 1B the cut on throws home. The chapter treats them as two jobs, not one.
- Slash and wheel live in drill pages, not the bunting/strategy concept pages. Used those drills; did not invent mechanics.
- “Steal on the pitcher, not the catcher” is not a KB heading. Built from `holding-runners-and-pickoffs` (timing, first move, 45-degree line) plus `baserunning-fundamentals`.
- Why higher levels bunt less: no run-expectancy numbers in the KB. Stayed qualitative (better defence, more damage per swing, out often costs more than it buys).
- SOLL Majors vs national Rule 7.13 leadoff conflict: followed the national rulebook, as the KB instructs.

## 7. Deviations

- `curriculum-t2.js` / `t3.js` were not on disk. Matched `curriculum-t1.js`.
- `ch13` has four `field` diagrams (standard, infield-in, dp-depth, no-doubles), not the minimum three.
- `ch14` has four `field` diagrams with `roles`, not the minimum three.
- `makeTheCall` cases carry both `situation` (widget brief) and `prompt` (t1 pattern) so either reader works.
- Cutoff/relay scored as `base` in `assignTheNine`, and that mapping is stated in the chapter. The baseball-app engine uses a fifth role (`cutoff`); the widget only has three.
- Extra KB pages listed above, beyond the brief’s per-chapter list.
- No shell, so no `node --check`. The reviewer owns that.
